title: BASE Resource
description: Progressive metadata for local-first BASE resources.

title.description: Strongly recommended for shared resources and discovery, but optional so personal Markdown can stay lightweight.

review_by.description: Date by which a human should re-read this resource (aging ontology). Consumed by `base doctor`.

valid_from.description: Start of validity for reference data (rates, price lists). Consumed by `base doctor` and the context pack.

valid_until.description: End of validity for reference data. Past this date, doctor flags it and the context pack annotates «périmé depuis …».

confidential.description: Set by a HUMAN, never inferred: this resource never leaves toward a remote model provider (egress control).

license.description: Machine-readable content licence for this resource (e.g. CC-BY-4.0, Apache-2.0). Makes per-resource licensing explicit, not just repo-wide.

compatibility.description: Tiers or clients this resource targets (e.g. navigateur, cli, mcp, studio). Declares where it is meant to apply; advisory, not enforced.

superseded_anchors.description: Where a renamed section went: { "<old-anchor>": "<current-anchor>" }. A section is cited as id#anchor and the anchor derives from the heading, so rewording a heading breaks the citations already written down. Each entry must name an anchor the document still has; one that resolves to nothing reads as not found, never as another section.

lang.description: Language of this edition (ISO 639-1). When absent, the file name suffix `<slug>.<lang>.md` answers instead; a language-neutral resource (a folder card, a figure record) declares neither.

translation_of.description: Id of the canonical resource this edition translates. Declared on the translation only: the canonical declares nothing, and the family resolves from either end.

attribution.description: The rule of use a collection declares for everything it holds, written on the folder's README.md card (e.g. «Written by Acme. Reuse only with this line.»). An MCP deployment that sets `mcp.attribution_prefix` returns the nearest such line with every read, so the rule travels with the content.

cite_as.description: The citation a passage of this resource travels with, as a human would write it (e.g. «Guide (2026), p. 4»).

source.description: Stable semantic reference to where the resource lives; concrete access belongs to connectors. For a converted document, it also names the printed pages behind the text.

pages.description: The printed pages this resource transcribes, in order.

image.description: Root-relative path to the page image of the original.

page_images.description: Root-relative path template for page images, with `{page}` or `{page:03}` (zero-padded) resolved for each entry of `pages`.

requires.description: Semantic resource dependencies used by processes and tools. This declares what a workflow needs; it does not grant access.

access.description: Expected use of the referenced resource by this workflow. Native permissions and BASE policy still decide whether the action can actually run.

purpose.description: Why the workflow needs this dependency. Context packs expose it as an explanatory note; it grants no access.

derived_from.description: Sources this document was written FROM (ids or root-relative paths). A summary never replaces its sources: this says where to go back to, and lets `base doctor` say when a source moved after the summary was written.

use_when.description: Routing signal: a short natural-language sentence describing WHEN to use this resource. Highest-signal field for the Router; optional and advisory (progressive metadata).

routing.description: Optional structured routing hints derived with the file. `examples` are real user phrasings (lift recall); `avoid_when` are counter-examples.
